## RTMB Sockeye Ricker

```{r}
#| echo: false
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
sox <- read.csv("../data/sockeye/SRDATA2026 1.csv")
stock <- read.csv("../data/sockeye/FC_StockInfo 2.csv")
sox <- sox %>% left_join(stock, by = "PopID")
sox <- sox %>% filter(!is.na(spawners), !is.na(recruits))
sox <- sox %>% group_by(PopName) %>% mutate(sd_spawners = sd(spawners),  spawners_scaled = spawners/sd_spawners) %>% ungroup()
```

```{r}
#| echo: true
library(RTMB)

sox$stock <- as.numeric(factor(sox$PopName))
nstocks <- max(sox$stock)
parameters <- list(
  alpha = runif(nstocks, 2, 5),
  logbeta = runif(nstocks, 0, 1),
  logsigma = runif(nstocks, 3, 5)
)

sox$logRS <- log(sox$recruits/sox$spawners)

negll <- function(pars){
  getAll(pars)
  beta <- exp(logbeta)
  sigma <- exp(logsigma)
  mu <- alpha[sox$stock] - beta[sox$stock]*sox$spawners_scaled
  -sum(dnorm(sox$logRS, mu, sigma[sox$stock], log = TRUE))
}
obj <- MakeADFun(func = negll, parameters = parameters, silent = TRUE)
```

## Find MLE

- Find minimum negative log likelihood
- Use `nlminb` by default and pass initial values, function, and gradient.

```{r}
#| echo: true

par_init <- obj$par + rnorm(length(obj$par))
mle <- nlminb(par_init, obj$fn, obj$gr)

## relist everything for convenience to access parameters by name
parList <- obj$env$parList(mle$par)
```

## Now What?

1. Check convergence
2. Transform parameters to real scale
3. Compute variance
4. Compute confidence intervals

## Convergence

- Check for error messages from optimization.
```{r}
#| echo: true

mle$convergence
mle$message
```

- Make sure all the gradient values are small
```{r}
#| echo: true

max(abs(obj$gr(mle$par)))
```

- Hessian should be positive definite. This one will be obvious if the variance can be computed.
```{r}
#| echo: true

## solve(obj$he(mle$par))
```


## Convergence

- If you are very thorough, you will try multiple starting points and make sure they all end up the same.

::: {#my-long-container style="height: 200px; border: 1px solid #ccc;"}
```{r}
#| echo: true

nll <- NULL
pars <- NULL
for( i in 1:50 ){
  par_init <- rnorm(length(obj$par), 0, 3)
  mle <- nlminb(par_init, obj$fn, obj$gr)
  if(mle$convergence == 0){
    pars <- cbind(pars, mle$par)
    nll <- c(nll, mle$objective)
  }
}
max(nll) - min(nll)
```
:::

## Transform Parameters

- `REPORT` to return value of variable
- `ADREPORT` to include uncertainty of variable
- `sdeport` will return standard deviations of parameters
- `as.list` of `sdreport` object will create a list of the parameters.

```{r}
#| echo: true

negll <- function(pars){
  getAll(pars)
  beta <- exp(logbeta)
  sigma <- exp(logsigma)
  beta_real <- beta*transform_beta
  ADREPORT(beta)
  mu <- alpha[sox$stock] - beta[sox$stock]*sox$spawners_scaled
  -sum(dnorm(sox$logRS, mu, sigma[sox$stock], log = TRUE))
}
transform_beta <- sox$spawners/sox$sd_spawners

obj <- MakeADFun(negll, parameters, silent = TRUE)
fit <- nlminb(obj$par, obj$fn, obj$gr)
sdr <- sdreport(obj, fit$par)
res <- summary(sdr, "fixed")
res_real <- summary(sdr, "report")
```


## Compute Variance

- Variance or standard deviation is approximated by inverse of Hessian of negative log-likelihood,

$$ 
  V(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}) = H^{-1}(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}).
$$

```{r}
#| echo: true

H <- obj$he(fit$par)
V <- solve(H)
std_err <- sqrt(diag(V))
max(abs(res[, "Std. Error"] - std_err))
```

## Compute Variance of Transformed Variables

- Delta Method can be used to compute standard error of transformed variables, for transformation $g$,

$$ 
  V(g(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\theta}})) = \nabla g V(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}) \nabla g'.
$$

- Showing to peak in 'black box' of how RTMB does this.

- For our example above:

\begin{align}
  g(\alpha) & = \alpha \\
  g'(\alpha) & = 1
\end{align}

\begin{align}
  g(\log \beta) & = \exp(\log \beta) = \beta \\
  g'(\log \beta) & = \exp(\log \beta) = \beta 
\end{align}

- Code it in R and compare with RTMB

::: {#my-long-container style="height: 200px; border: 1px solid #ccc;"}
```{r}
#| echo: true

which_alpha <- grepl("alpha", names(obj$par))
par_real <- MakeTape(
\(x){
  x[!which_alpha] <- exp(x[!which_alpha]);
  return(x)}, obj$par)
g <- par_real$jacobian(fit$par)

V_real <- g %*% V %*% t(g)
std_err_real <- sqrt(diag(V_real))
max(abs(res_real[, "Std. Error"] - std_err_real[grepl("beta", names(obj$par))]))
```
:::

## Confidence Interval

- Typical format of 95% confidence interval ('Wald')
  $$
    \widehat{\beta} \pm z_{0.025} \, \text{sd}(\widehat{\alpha})
  $$
- $z$ is a standard normal distribution. For a linear regression we know that the slope terms are $t$ distributed

- Quantiles / confidence intervals are transformation invariant (i.e. you can just transform the CI to process for real scale)

::: {#my-long-container style="height: 200px; border: 1px solid #ccc;"}
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: "center"

estimates <- as.list(sdr, "Est") ## parameter estimates
std.error <- as.list(sdr, "Std. Error") ## parameter estimates
logbeta <- estimates$logbeta
sd_logbeta <- std.error$logbeta
nlbeta <- length(logbeta)
low_lbeta <- logbeta + qnorm(0.025)*sd_logbeta
high_lbeta <- logbeta + qnorm(0.975)*sd_logbeta

stocks <- levels(factor(sox$PopName))
plot(logbeta, pch = 16, ylim = c(-6, 2), xlab = "stock", ylab = "log(beta)")
arrows(1:nlbeta, low_lbeta, 1:nlbeta, high_lbeta, length = 0.1, 
  angle = 90, code = 3, col = "black", lwd = 2)
```
:::

## Confidence Interval Transformed

- Compare confidence interval transformed vs transforming first and then computing confidence interval.

::: {#my-long-container style="height: 300px; border: 1px solid #ccc;"}
```{r}
#| echo: true
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: "center"

low_tr <- exp(low_lbeta)
high_tr <- exp(high_lbeta)

beta <- as.list(sdr, "Est", report=TRUE)$beta ## parameter estimates
sd_beta <- as.list(sdr, "Std. Error", report=TRUE)$beta ## parameter estimates
low_r <- beta + qnorm(0.025)*sd_beta
high_r <- beta + qnorm(0.975)*sd_beta
nbeta <- length(beta)

plot(exp(logbeta), pch = 16, ylim = c(-0.5, 1.5), xlab = "stock", ylab = "beta")
arrows(1:nbeta, low_tr, 1:nbeta, high_tr, length = 0.1, angle = 90, code = 3, col = "black", lwd = 2)
points(1:nbeta+0.25, beta, pch = 16, col='blue')
arrows(1:nbeta+0.25, low_r, 1:nbeta+0.25, high_r, length = 0.1, angle = 90, code = 3, col = "blue", lwd = 2)
```
:::

## Profile Confidence Interval

- Best confidence interval but computationally demanding
- Find 95% area under profile likelihood
- Profile likelihood traverses a single parameter values, finds MLE for other values.
- Takes into account skew of distribution etc.

```{r}
#| echo: true
prof <- TMB::tmbprofile(obj, name = 31, trace = FALSE)
plot(prof)
abline(v = fit$par[31], col = 'red', lty = 2)
prof_int <- confint(prof)
```

```{r}
#| echo: true

plot(1:3, rep(beta[12], 3), ylim = c(-0.5, 1.5), pch = 16, xlab = "Interval Type", xaxt = "n")
axis(1, at = 1:3, labels = c("Transform", "Real Scale", "Profile"))

arrows(1:3, c(low_tr[12], low_r[12], exp(prof_int[1])), 1:3, 
  c(high_tr[12], high_r[12], exp(prof_int[2])), length = 0.1, angle = 90, 
  code = 3, col = "black", lwd = 2)
```

## Bootstrapped Confidence Interval

- Declare data as `OBS` to let RTMB recognize it as data.
- Do a data update so that you don't have to retape each time `DataEval`

::: {#my-long-container style="height: 600px; border: 1px solid #ccc;"}
```{r}
#| echo: true

negll <- function(pars){
  getAll(pars, data, warn=FALSE)
  logRS <- DataEval(\(x){boot$logRS}) ## Updates the data.
  logRS <- OBS(logRS)
  beta <- exp(logbeta)
  sigma <- exp(logsigma)
  beta_real <- beta[stock]*transform_beta
  REPORT(beta)
  mu <- alpha[stock] - beta[stock]*spawners_scaled
  logRS %~% dnorm(mu, sigma[stock]) ## Alternative way to define likelihood...
}

data <- list(stock = sox$stock, 
  spawners_scaled = sox$spawners_scaled, 
  transform_beta = sox$spawners/sox$sd_spawners
  )
boot <- list(logRS = sox$logRS)

obj <- MakeADFun(negll, parameters, silent = TRUE)
fit <- nlminb(obj$par, obj$fn, obj$gr)

boot.pars <- NULL
for( i in 1:1000 ){
  boot$logRS <- obj$simulate(fit$par)$logRS
  newfit <- nlminb(obj$par, obj$fn, obj$gr)
  newbeta <- obj$report(newfit$par)$beta
  boot.pars <- cbind(boot.pars, newbeta)
}
boot.ci <- apply(boot.pars, 1, quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.975) )

plot(1:4, rep(beta[12], 4), ylim = c(-0.5, 1.5), pch = 16, xlab = "Interval Type", xaxt = "n")
axis(1, at = 1:4, labels = c("Transform", "Real Scale", "Profile", "Bootstrapped"))

arrows(1:4, c(low_tr[12], low_r[12], exp(prof_int[1]), boot.ci[1,12]), 1:4, 
  c(high_tr[12], high_r[12], exp(prof_int[2]), boot.ci[2,12]), 
  length = 0.1, angle = 90, 
  code = 3, col = "black", lwd = 2)
```
:::

## Practical

- Run through your version of the sockeye code and create confidence intervals for different parameters.
- Compute residuals for this model?
- Use `DHARMa` to calculate randomized quantile residuals?
- Can you improve the model?

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

res_dharma <- createDHARMa(
  simulatedResponse = sim_matrix, ## Each column a new simulation
  observedResponse = observed_y,  ## Observed data
  fittedPredictedResponse = predicted_y,  ## Fitted values (mu)
  integerResponse = FALSE
)

plot(res_dharma)
```

## End of Module

- Take home: 
  * RTMB does not require many changes to do maximum likelihood estimation
  * Lots more to think about than using a function in R like `lm`
  * Can use `REPORT` and `ADREPORT` to get key values
  * Confidence intervals can be a little tricky, transform the CI or bootstrap/profile.

- Questions?
